purpose: Canonical variable registry and loop alignment across all six Team Zig contributors. The team's divergent thinking produced six independently-named variable sets; this is the join that makes them comparable.
method: Each canonical variable carries every contributor's own wording as an alias. Aliasing is judgement and is listed in full so it can be disputed. Loops are aligned only after their variables resolve to registry entries.
rule: Alignment records that contributors described the same construct. It does not merge their evidence, and it does not upgrade any claim's epistemic status.

variables.label: Realized value
variables.definition: Value the member actually obtains and can use. Points sitting unspent are value earned, not value realized.

variables.label: Sustained engagement
variables.definition: Repeat use of the program over time — a pattern of earning, checking, redeeming and returning.

variables.label: Transactions & participation
variables.definition: What members actually spend and do through the program — swipes, partner purchases, activations, redemptions.

variables.label: Permissioned signal richness
variables.definition: How much the system is permitted to know about a member, and how useful that knowledge is.

variables.label: Decisioning relevance
variables.definition: How well the system picks the right opportunity for the right member at the right moment.

aliases.wording: Personalization toward a segment of one

variables.label: Relevant, visible opportunities
variables.definition: Worthwhile opportunities an eligible member can discover and understand.

variables.label: Program trust
variables.definition: Confidence that the program will reliably convert its promises into usable value.

variables.label: Redemption rate
variables.definition: The share of issued points members actually spend.

variables.label: Breakage revenue
variables.definition: Money the program keeps because points were never redeemed.

variables.label: Offer margin headroom
variables.definition: How much the program can afford to give away and still hit margin.

variables.label: Offer generosity & point value
variables.definition: How much a point is worth and how good the deals are.

variables.label: Unresolved or uncertain value
variables.definition: Worthwhile value that was promised but has not visibly arrived, or whose state the member cannot determine.

aliases.wording: Missing / expiring states in the ledger

variables.label: Member uncertainty & friction
variables.definition: Delay, effort and doubt the member absorbs while trying to progress value.

variables.label: Detection & resolution effort
variables.definition: Work done to identify an interruption, explain it, and resolve or route it.

variables.label: Reward status visibility & clarity
variables.definition: Whether earned, pending, posted, redeemed, missing and expiring states are accurate and legible to the member.

variables.label: Reward-processing demand
variables.definition: Volume and complexity of earning, posting, redemption, fulfilment and support activity.

variables.label: Operational load
variables.definition: Workload on the capabilities and teams delivering program value.

variables.label: Personalization intensity
variables.definition: How hard the system leans on member data to target offers.

variables.label: Perceived intrusion
variables.definition: How closely watched the personalization makes a member feel.

variables.label: Consent granted
variables.definition: Whether members agree to this use of their data — and keep agreeing.

variables.label: Member–client overlap
variables.definition: People who are both Blue Rewards members and BMO banking customers.

variables.label: Combined signals
variables.definition: What can be seen when a person is viewed as member and client together.

variables.label: Partner-attributable spend
variables.definition: Spend at a partner brand the partner can see came from Blue Rewards.

variables.label: Anchor partner retention
variables.definition: Whether big-category weekly partners stay.

variables.label: Earn & redeem breadth
variables.definition: How many everyday places a member can earn and spend.

variables.label: Everyday relevance
variables.definition: Whether the program shows up in ordinary weekly life.

variables.label: Member goal achievement
variables.definition: Progress against a goal the member has stated.

variables.label: Demonstrated value of connecting
variables.definition: Concrete, visible proof that linking an account or granting data returns something the member can use.

variables.label: Channel & data fragmentation
variables.definition: Value, status and opportunity split across channels and systems that do not resolve to one view.

variables.label: Engagement & revenue
variables.definition: Program revenue produced by sustained engagement.

loops.name: Relevance flywheel
loops.summary: Value members actually get keeps them engaged; engagement produces permissioned signal; signal improves relevance; relevance produces more realized value.

joann.name: Relevance flywheel
joann.note: Collapses opportunity surfacing into the relevance→value link.

sly.name: Value Realization and Learning Flywheel
sly.note: Adds trust as an explicit step.

henry.name: Value Realization Flywheel
henry.note: Identical to Sly's, node for node, in different words.

lia.name: Reinforcing Loop (more engagement)
lia.note: Four-node compression; no trust or capture step.

loops.finding: Five of six contributors independently drew this loop. It is the same causal structure at four different resolutions, not five different theories.

loops.name: Program economics — the breakage brake
loops.summary: Redemption is what members want, but the programme is funded on points nobody uses. Redemption up, breakage down, headroom down, generosity down, value reaching members down.

joann.name: Program economics
joann.note: Full five-step form with the inverse link named.

josh.name: Personalized Value & Breakage
josh.note: CONFIRMED BY JOSH, 10 Sept. Originally resolved from the 5 Sept working session: Josh states increasing personalization 'increases less breakage for BMO, like it's not great financially'. Personalization to breakage is the inverse link. Enters the same brake through personalization rather than through redemption.

loops.finding: Three contributors found the same brake by three different routes - Joann through redemption, Ola through scale investment, Josh through personalization. All three land on the same inverse link. It is the only brake where the inverse link is arithmetic rather than behavioural — a point that gets used cannot also go unused.

loops.name: Trust & consent — the permission brake
loops.summary: Personalization runs on permission it can spend. Push intensity too hard and members feel watched, consent narrows, signal thins, relevance falls.

joann.name: Trust & consent
joann.note: Framed as the cap on how hard R1 can be pushed.

lia.name: Balancing Loop (keeps things in check)
lia.note: Routes through trust explicitly before consent.

josh.name: Progressive consent (JL02)
josh.note: Not drawn as a loop; appears as a leverage point on the same mechanism.

loops.finding: Two contributors drew this independently and a third proposed intervening on it. It is the only brake that acts on the flywheel's fuel rather than its output.

loops.name: Value gap — the delivery brake
loops.summary: Value that was promised but did not visibly arrive creates uncertainty and friction, which triggers detection and resolution effort, which restores clarity and realized value — reducing the unresolved value that started it.

henry.name: Reward Value Gap Correction
henry.note: The only contributor to draw the correction as a closed loop.

sly.name: Operational Friction and Capacity Constraint
sly.note: Same failure, different cause: capacity not keeping up with volume.

joann.name: The six-state ledger
joann.note: Modelled as a state machine with one capability per failure mode rather than as a loop.

loops.finding: Henry and Sly describe the same breakdown from opposite ends — Henry from the member's uncertainty, Sly from the operation's capacity. Both end at unresolved value reducing realization and trust.

loops.name: Conversion flywheel
loops.summary: Engagement produces member-client overlap; overlap produces combined signal; combined signal improves relevance; relevance produces realized value.

joann.name: Conversion flywheel
joann.note: Proposed as the replacement revenue source if breakage comes off the scorecard.

josh.name: Goal-linked conversion
josh.note: FROM TRANSCRIPT, 5 Sept: 'how do we convert a better loyalty experience... into broadening the deeper relationship with BMO through their products and services... instead of measuring it, maybe we could force that'. His goal construct is the mechanism - rewards goals and financial goals set together.

loops.finding: Joann and Josh independently reached the same conclusion, and said so to each other on the call: 'you and I had on the same, like that cross-selling of products and services'. Both also propose it as the answer to breakage - the only revenue source in the team's set that grows when redemption grows.

loops.name: Partner coverage
loops.summary: The flywheel on the supply side. Engagement produces attributable partner spend, which retains anchor partners, which widens earn-and-redeem breadth, which makes the programme part of ordinary weekly life.
loops.finding: The only loop anyone claims is currently spinning in the wrong direction, which makes it the least redundant and least examined part of the team's set.

loops.name: Reliability and trust
loops.summary: Investment in reliable, visible status produces trust; trust produces engagement; engagement funds further investment. This loop routes through status visibility rather than through relevance.
loops.finding: Ola is the only contributor to close reliability into a loop - and it is the loop Joann's six-state ledger acts on directly. The team's most-specified product feature drives the team's least-discussed loop.

loops.name: Connected-data adoption
loops.summary: Showing a member what connecting an account would return gives them a reason to connect; connection enriches combined signal; richer signal improves relevance; relevance produces realized value, which is itself the next proof.

josh.name: Consumer-Driven Banking Awareness & Adoption
josh.note: DERIVED from JL02 prose and CORROBORATED by the 5 Sept transcript, where Josh names the hook as cash and the barrier as low trust: 'Department of Finance has done surveys. It's low trust on consumer driven banking... how do you incentivize people to give that data? For me, what I've come up with and seen is its cash.'

derivation.basis: Josh states the chain almost completely in JL02: a value preview gives members a reason to participate, and progressive consent helps the loop gain enough participation to produce useful experiences and visible proof. Reason-to-participate to consent to signal to experiences to proof is a closed reinforcing path.
derivation.assumption: The return arrow from visible proof back to the value preview was the only inferred element. Josh confirmed it on 10 Sept.

loops.finding: Josh named this loop out loud and gave both its hook (cash value) and its barrier (low trust in consumer-driven banking). Zero negative links, consistent with his reinforcing label. Overlaps the trust-and-consent brake at consent granted.

loops.name: Fragmentation and disengagement
loops.summary: Fragmented channels and data raise the effort of finding and tracking value; effort suppresses engagement; less engagement thins signal; thinner signal degrades relevance; degraded relevance leaves the experience more fragmented still.

josh.name: Digital Friction & Engagement
josh.note: DERIVED from the loop name plus JL03. Josh supplied neither variables nor polarities.

derivation.basis: The name pairs friction with engagement, and JL03 treats fragmentation as the thing to restructure. Two negative links - friction suppressing engagement, relevance reducing fragmentation - give an even count, consistent with a reinforcing label.
derivation.assumption: The whole structure was constructed from a loop name plus parity arithmetic, then approved rather than authored. Josh confirmed it on 10 Sept, which settles the direction question but does not turn a construction into independent evidence. Treat the variables and polarities as a shared working model rather than as Josh's prior analysis.

loops.finding: Approved by Josh on 10 Sept. It is still the only loop in the team set whose variables and polarities nobody stated before this consolidation proposed them - neither his document nor the 5 Sept session describes the mechanism. Approval records agreement, not evidence.
